history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Sikh gurdwara, keep-or-drop decision needed. Gurdwara Nanakmatta Sahib is one of the three holiest Sikh places in Uttarakhand (with Hemkunt Sahib and Reetha Sahib). Formerly called Gorakhmata, a centre of the Siddh-jogis of Guru Gorakhnath, it was renamed Nanakmatta after Guru Nanak Dev visited during his third Udasi in 1514 and held his famous religious dialogue (Siddh-Gost, recorded in the Guru Granth Sahib) with the yogis; legend says the earth itself answered 'Nanakmatta, Nanakmatta' when the Siddhas challenged his claim to the land. Baba Almast Ji later preached here until expelled by the jogis, who burnt the sacred pipal tree; Guru Hargobind restored Sikh possession. Surviving relics include Bhora Sahib, Dhoona Sahib, Baoli Sahib and the revived 500-year-old pipal tree. The shrine stands beside the Deoha stream, dammed into the Nanak Sagar reservoir. CSV town corrected from 'Udham Singh Nagar' to Nanakmatta; the town itself is named after the gurdwara.

name: Gurudwara Nanakmatta Sahib
town_description: Nanakmatta is a small town in Udham Singh Nagar district named after the gurdwara, set between Khatima and Sitarganj. The Deoha stream here is dammed into the Nanak Sagar reservoir (dam completed in 1962), a popular picnic and boating spot that draws visitors alongside the shrine. It is also an Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly constituency.

travel.railway: Khatima Railway Station, about 15 km to the east
travel.road: On the Khatima-Tanakpur road between Khatima and Sitarganj; buses to Khatima available from Delhi (ISBT Anand Vihar)
